CIEM 5140.title: Construction Project Delivery
CIEM 5140.description: The course would cover Principle of Project Management, Contractor Management, Public Works Development, Consultant Management & Engineering proposal, Design & Build, BOT & PPP, Project Finance, Project Risk Management, Project Partnering, Value Management, Safety Management, Environment Management, Case Studies.
cilos: Define the construction industry and different stages in a construction project.
Illustrate current HKSAR Work Bureau Guidelines, Circulars and Construction Industry Code of Practices by means of real-life industry Case Studies.
Specify the responsibilities of Consultants and Contractors in Construction Safety Management, Environmental Management and Project Management.
Perform Risk Management, Value Engineering and Partnering Approach in a construction project.
Formulate and resolve the latest Construction Procurement Strategy.
Identify the funding source in Public and Private infrastructure project.

CIEM 5160.title: Construction Financial Management
CIEM 5160.description: Estimate, tendering strategy, budgetary control, contract account, cash flow management, depreciation, taxation effects, annual reports, strategic management, benefit cost analysis, life cycle costing, value engineering.
cilos: Identify the characteristics of the construction industry.
Identify fundamental knowledge in construction project planning.
Estimate construction costs.
Control construction costs.
Conduct cash flow analysis of construction projects.
Analyze the financial and operational performance of a construction company.

CIEM 5170.title: Building Information Modeling and Smart Construction
CIEM 5170.description: This course will cover the fundamental and technical aspects of building information modeling (BIM) and smart construction. Topics include BIM model creation and sharing, model-based analyses, clash detection, BIM standards and interoperability, BIM project execution plan, BIM for infrastructure, visualization technologies, data mining and knowledge management, decision support system, construction informatics, sensing technologies, and construction robotics.
cilos: Identify the principles of building information modeling (BIM) and the current technologies for BIM.
Leverage software for building information modeling and construction management.
Model and represent various kinds of information in the construction industry.
Perform data processing and mining for knowledge discovery.
Design and leverage database systems for managing information and supporting construction management.

CIEM 5180.title: Construction Technology for Civil Engineering Works
CIEM 5180.description: This course intends to provide an overview of modern construction technology for civil engineering works with special attention paid to recent development trends and major construction works in Hong Kong. The course starts with the design/construction interface and focuses on the Contractor’s perspective. In particular, ground improvements, reclamation works, excavation-lateral support system and modular construction as well as digital construction will be highlighted. With an aim to help students who have limited exposure to construction practice, this course uses a Capstone project to help the students to form a comprehensive view of a construction project, including site layouts, construction practice, contract type, and construction methods. Students would be required to apply the knowledge learned to describe a real-life construction project and critically analyze the construction activities.
cilos: Identify the routines of local construction practice with an international exposure.
Professionally describe a construction project and its main elements and characteristics.
Explain the connections between design and construction.
Analyze the full set of construction activities including both underground and superstructure works.
Identify key construction methods and technologies for both permanent and temporary works.
Be aware of the current construction practice and its future trends.
Describe ways of improving construction process by innovations.
Interpret the contract, commercial, planning and HSE (Health, Safety and Environmental) perspectives of a construction project.

CIEM 5190.title: Alternative Dispute Resolution: Law and Practice
CIEM 5190.description: This course provides a complete introduction to the subject of dispute resolution in construction and engineering including: the legal background to and foundation for contractual claims and disputes; standard forms and conditions of contract; the various modes of alternative dispute resolution (ADR); the nature of, practice and hearings before ADR tribunals; and the role of engineers serving as expert witnesses and adjudicators.
cilos: Identify construction law and practice in context.
Distinguish between and assess various standard forms and conditions of contract.
Prepare, evaluate and defend construction claims and disputes.
Describe and evaluate numerous alternative dispute resolution (ADR) processes.
Identify the law and practice of dispute resolution hearings.
Analyze the role of engineers as advocates, expert witnesses and fact-finders in dispute resolution.

CIEM 5240.title: Advanced Concrete Technology
CIEM 5240.description: Green concrete, concrete rheology and its tuning, concrete failure and fracture mechanics, durability of concrete under various environments, steel corrosion in concrete, non-destructive evaluation of concrete, concrete repair, special concretes (high strength, high stiffness, fiber reinforced, lightweight).
cilos: Describe the proper selection of concrete raw materials to enhance greenness.
Identify factors affecting concrete rheology, failure and durability.
Explain steel corrosion in concrete, including its control and inspection.
Define non-destructive methods for concrete members.
Explain repair methods and repair materials for concrete members.
Analyze the design and application of various special concretes.

CIEM 5310.title: Structural Analysis and Design of Tall Buildings
CIEM 5310.description: Integrated treatment of analytical methods and technical aspects in design of tall building structures, including structural modeling, frames, shear walls, outrigger-braced systems, core-walls, tubular structures, and special topics.
cilos: Recognize the engineering mechanics and structural modelling techniques on which the analysis and design of tall building structures are based.
Identify the structural behaviour and performance of different forms of tall buildings and the analysis and design principles of tall building structures.
Conduct analysis and preliminary design of different types of tall building structures.
Apply the modern engineering software ETABS for the analysis and design of tall building structures.

CIEM 5311.title: Building Aerodynamics and Wind-Resistant Design of High-Rise Structures
CIEM 5311.description: Global wind climate, extreme wind analysis, wind structures near ground, bluff body aerodynamics, wind loads on building structures, wind-induced vibrations and mitigations, wind tunnel test techniques, and wind loading codes.
cilos: Describe the characteristics of wind, wind structure near ground and topographical effects on wind.
Identify typhoon structures and perform simple typhoon simulation.
Determine the alongwind and crosswind forces of a structure and the wind-induced structural responses.
Analyze dynamic problem of buildings subject to different dynamic loads.
Identify the attributes of an effective wind-resistant design.
Perform a tall building design following Hong Kong and Australian wind codes.
Recognize and appreciate various types of wind tunnel testing techniques.

CIEM 5320.title: Computer Aided Design Optimization of Tall Buildings
CIEM 5320.description: This course provides consolidated theoretical background and practical knowledge on the analysis, computer aided modeling and design optimization of modern tall building structures. Topics include behavior of different forms of tall building structures; finite element modeling and analysis; principles and practice of structural optimization for tall building design.
cilos: Recognize the challenges of building taller structures and the development of modern structural systems for tall buildings.
Define computer modelling principles and applications of finite element analysis for tall building structures.
Describe advanced knowledge of numerical optimization methodology for structural design of tall buildings.
Apply the state-of-the-art computer based techniques for engineering analysis and design optimization of real-life typical high-rise building projects.

CIEM 5320.title: Computer Aided Design Optimization of Tall Buildings
CIEM 5320.description: This course provides consolidated theoretical background and practical knowledge on the analysis, computer aided modeling and design optimization of modern tall building structures. Topics include behavior of different forms of tall building structures; finite element modeling and analysis; principles and practice of structural optimization for tall building design.
cilos: Recognize the challenges of building taller structures and the development of modern structural systems for tall buildings.
Define computer modelling principles and applications of finite element analysis for tall building structures.
Describe advanced knowledge of numerical optimization methodology for structural design of tall buildings.
Apply the state-of-the-art computer based techniques for engineering analysis and design optimization of real-life typical high-rise building projects.

CIEM 5380.title: Bridge Engineering
CIEM 5380.description: This course is focused on the bridge superstructure analysis and design using limit states design method. The main objectives of this course include the introduction of limit states design method; discussion of design philosophy and code requirements; as well as analysis and design examples using limit states design method.
cilos: Define different bridge construction methods.
Define different bridge structural forms.
Describe how bridge construction/erection methodology affects bridge design.
Select appropriate bridge form with a given site constraint.
Estimate preliminary material quantity required for a bridge project.

CIEM 5390.title: Coastal Structures Design
CIEM 5390.description: The course will cover basic wave characteristics, linear wave theory, wave transformation processes, wind-wave generation, coastal processes, wave-structure interaction, design procedures and requirements for coastal structures such as seawalls, breakwaters and beaches.
cilos: Recognize the challenges that confront costal engineers.
Integrate various approaches and tools to analyze and design costal structures.
Describe and apply the principles that underpin the estimation of wave loads on structures.

CIEM 5410.title: Risk Assessment and Contaminated Land Cleanup
CIEM 5410.description: Innovative technologies for land and groundwater remediation, site investigation, risk assessment, and local case studies on land decontamination such as Kai Tak Airport, Penny's Bay, North Tsing Yi will be included.
cilos: Describe the regulations for contaminated land management in Hong Kong.
Assess the potential risks associated with land contamination.
Evaluate and compare the applications of various remediation technologies.
Design cost-effective remediation technology to decontaminate a site.
Identify real applications from case studies.

CIEM 5420.title: Biological Waste Treatment and Management
CIEM 5420.description: Principles of secondary, biological treatment processes, including sewage sand filters, trickling filters, activated sludge plants, lagoons, ponds, rotating biological contactors, aerobic and anaerobic digesters, and biological nutrient removal. Management of waste treatment systems and works.
cilos: Define the fundamental and advanced knowledge of current solid wastes and wastewater treatment and disposal systems and their problems in Hong Kong and beyond.
Identify key problems of water and wastewater treatment processes, and propose fundamental engineering and management solution.
Professionally judge and assess the advantages and disadvantages of various sewage treatment technologies such as MEL, AGS, BABY, Anammox, etc.
Select the treatment processes/technologies for meeting a more stringent discharge requirement for water pollution control with focus of tertiary treatment.
Design basic treatment units and systems for municipal wastewater treatment.

CIEM 5460.title: Design and Management of Physico/Chemical Processes of Environmental Engineering
CIEM 5460.description: Principles, design and management practices of physico/chemical treatment processes for removing contaminants from drinking water and municipal wastewaters; includes coagulation and flocculation, sedimentation, air flotation, centrifugation, filtration, membrane, air stripping, carbon adsorption, disinfection, chemical oxidation processes, operation management and residual management.
cilos: Describe the fundamental and advanced knowledge of physical-chemical processes in the environmental engineering field.
Identify problems and propose feasible engineering or management solutions during the operation of water and wastewater treatment processes.
Design the physical-chemical unit processes and integrate them to systems for water and wastewater treatment.
Analyze major factors impacting physical-chemical treatment systems and provide management strategies.

CIEM 5480.title: Wastewater Treatment and Reuse
CIEM 5480.description: Theory and conceptual design of key unit processes and unit operations in domestic wastewater treatment and reuse with emphasis on applications of compact and advanced treatment technologies.
cilos: Identify and evaluate the environmental problems through reviewing the key water pollution parameters of water and wastewater.
Select the sewage treatment levels and processes required to meet the discharge requirements and to protect the receiving water bodies.
Carry out the process design for municipal sewage treatment plant including primary, chemically enhanced primary, secondary and sludge treatment.
Evaluate the operational problems and identify practical solutions during the operation of the municipal sewage treatment plants.
Select the tertiary treatment processes required for meeting a more stringent discharge requirement for water pollution control.
Select the treatment processes and identify the key design parameters and monitoring requirements for wastewater reuse.

CIEM 5620.title: Travel Demand Analysis
CIEM 5620.description: Overview of transportation planning process, population/employment forecasting techniques, discrete choice models, simplified transportation demand models.
cilos: Evaluate the advanced theories and methods of traffic and transportation engineering and transportation systems planning.
Utilize mathematical or quantitative methods to model components of transportation system.
Identify transportation system planning and management problems and propose feasible solutions.
Apply key transportation planning principles to the analysis, modeling and operation of transportation system, including traffic impact analysis and transportation demand forecasting.

CIEM 5630.title: Traffic Control Fundamentals and Practice
CIEM 5630.description: Traffic flow fundamentals; microscopic and macroscopic traffic flow characteristics; principle and theory of traffic signal; essential modeling techniques; various traffic signal control models.
cilos: Analyze principles involved in the design of traffic control.
Apply traffic control principles to model signalized junctions.
Design signalized junctions based on the Hong Kong practices.
Develop advanced control methods based on dynamic traffic flow fundamentals.

CIEM 5630.title: Traffic Control Fundamentals and Practice
CIEM 5630.description: Traffic flow fundamentals; microscopic and macroscopic traffic flow characteristics; principle and theory of traffic signal; essential modeling techniques; various traffic signal control models.
cilos: Analyze principles involved in the design of traffic control.
Apply traffic control principles to model signalized junctions.
Design signalized junctions based on the Hong Kong practices.
Develop advanced control methods based on dynamic traffic flow fundamentals.

CIEM 5720.title: Advanced Foundation Design
CIEM 5720.description: Current practice of foundation design and analysis, including design and analysis of bulkheads, deep excavation, tieback systems, tunneling in soft ground, buried conduits, lateral pile loading, pier foundations.
cilos: Identify basic performance requirements for foundations.
Define fundamental soil mechanics principles for foundation engineering design and construction.
Recognize the uncertainties throughout the site investigation, design and construction process, and how the uncertainties are handled in limit state design.
Design common types of foundations (shallow foundations, piles, returning walls, soil nails, offshore foundations etc.).
Conduct construction quality assurance.
Design new types of foundations (wind turbine foundations, energy piles etc.) based on first principles.

CIEM 5740.title: Computer Methods for Slope Engineering
CIEM 5740.description: This course aims to teach students to apply knowledge of soil mechanics and numerical methods for analysis and design of slope stability. The course covers mechanisms of slope failures, shear strength of soils, transient seepage analysis, major methodologies on slope stability analysis, and use of popular computer software programs for slope stability analysis, including SLOPE/W & SEEP/W and PLAXIS 2D.
cilos: Explain shear strength of soils and methods for slope stability analysis.
Evaluate soil and rock properties from laboratory tests and field data.
Apply different methods for evaluating the stability of soil slopes.
Use basic geotechnical software packages for stability analysis of soil slopes.
Analyze the stability of engineering soil slopes for safe design.

CIEM 5760.title: Engineering Geology and Rock Mechanics
CIEM 5760.description: The course provides fundamental knowledge in engineering geology and rock mechanics as applied to rock engineering design and practice. Topics include: major rock types, weathering process and local geological setting; mapping geologic structures and stereonet analysis; rock mass classification, stress-strain-strength properties of rock mass and joints; analysis and design methods for rock slopes, rock foundations and underground tunnels. A field trip will be arranged to visit Hong Kong GeoPark.
cilos: Identify local geological setting and geological process.
Identify major rock types including weathered rock profiles.
Map geologic structures and analyze discontinuities using stereonet.
Classify rock mass.
Describe stress-strain-strength behaviours of rock and joint.
Analyze slope stability, underground opening and foundation in rocks.

CIEM 5770.title: Unsaturated Soil Mechanics and Engineering
CIEM 5770.description: Fundamental principles, stress state variables, steady-state and transient flows, theory of shear strength and its measurements, soil stiffness, plastic and limit equilibrium analyses of earth pressures, slope stability and bearing capacity, critical state framework, instrumentation, engineering applications on slopes including static liquefaction of loose fill slopes, foundations, forensic studies such as slope failures.
cilos: Define the fundamental principles and advanced concepts of unsaturated soil mechanics.
Design and carry out laboratory and field tests for determining unsaturated soil properties.
Apply key principles of unsaturated soil mechanics to analyze and design geotechnical and geo-environmental structures such as landfill, pavement, foundation and slope.
Effectively communicate unsaturated soil mechanics and engineering to a range of audiences in a professional manner.

CIEM 5790.title: Slope Engineering and Management
CIEM 5790.description: This course will introduce in detail the slope safety management system in Hong Kong, including its background, past development, as well as its key components, e.g. geotechnical control and landslide prevention and mitigation programme. The course will also cover basic knowledge on engineering geology, Hong Kong landslides, fundamentals and methods of slope stability assessment, slope stabilisation and landslide mitigation measures as well as the advanced subjects of quantitative risk assessments and use of novel technologies in landslide assessment.
cilos: Recognize the background and past development of the slope safety management system in Hong Kong and describe the two key components of slope safety management system in Hong Kong, viz. (a) geotechnical control, and (b) landslide prevention and mitigation programme.
Describe the geology of Hong Kong, common types of landslides in Hong Kong and their key causal factors.
Analyze stability condition of slopes.
Analyze mobility of landslide debris.
Undertake design of common slope stabilisation works.
Undertake design of common landslide mitigation works.
Conduct quantitative risk assessment for use in slope safety management.

CIEM 5810.title: Engineering Risk, Reliability and Decision
CIEM 5810.description: Bayesian methods, reliability evaluation, system reliability, reliability-based design, probabilistic risk analysis, probabilistic observational methods, Monte Carlo Simulation, Fault and Event Tree models, elementary utility theory, decision with multiple objectives. Emphasis will be placed on applications. Practical examples will be used extensively to demonstrate application of these methods.
cilos: Identify the fundamental knowledge in probability and statistics.
Develop basic skill sets to perform probabilistic calculations with commercial toolboxes.
Define the concepts of engineering risk assessment and decision making.
Conduct useful analyses related to the subject, such as Monte Carlo Simulation.

CIEM 6000.title: Topics in Civil Infrastructural Engineering and Management
CIEM 6000.description: Selected topics of current interest. May be repeated for credit if different topics are covered.
cilos: Identify the fundamental knowledge in different areas related to the course topic.
Describe advanced theories and methods related to the course topic.
Formulate and solve problems in the various areas of the course topic.
Apply theories and methods to practical implementations.

CIEM 6000-6010.title: Topics in Civil Infrastructural Engineering and Management
CIEM 6000-6010.description: Selected topics of current interest. May be repeated for credit if different topics are covered.
cilos: Identify the fundamental knowledge in different areas related to the course topic.
Describe advanced theories and methods related to the course topic.
Formulate and solve problems in the various areas of the course topic.
Apply theories and methods to practical implementations.

CIEM 6980.title: MSc Project
CIEM 6980.description: An independent project carried out under the supervision of a faculty member.
cilos: Develop and apply self-learning and task management skills to effectively manage an independent project.
Critically analyze a selected topic to identify, formulate and solve problems and apply solutions to practical implementations.
Communicate effectively in writing, using accurate technical and scientific terminology, and demonstrating logical organization of relevant content and information.

Communicate effectively in oral presentation, demonstrating logical organization of relevant content and information, using appropriate style, pacing and body language, proper handling of questions, and effective time management.
